rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient covering the full solvent-strength range at mid temperature to reveal the retention spread, any missing late eluters, and overall peak density. This gives a balanced first map of the mixture for subsequent optimization.

All 10 compounds eluted with baseline resolution and substantial spare resolution, so the main opportunity is to reduce analysis time. Shortening the gradient while keeping composition range and temperature fixed should test how far runtime can be compressed before the closest cluster around peaks 5–7 becomes limiting.

The 12 min gradient is fast but over-compresses the central cluster, with the 6/7 pair dropping below acceptable resolution. A modest increase in gradient time should restore separation there while likely keeping the run short enough to preserve or improve CRF.

The only limiting issue remains the same central pair, and increasing tG from 12 to 14 min improved its resolution from 0.82 to 1.20 while keeping zero time penalty. A further small increase to 16 min is the most direct test for reaching full resolution without yet risking a meaningful time cost.

At 16 min full resolution is achieved but with slight time penalty, while 14 min is close and currently best overall. A small temperature decrease may selectively improve the critical 6/7 separation enough to keep the faster 14 min method while preserving the favorable runtime.

Lowering temperature worsened selectivity, so return to 40 C and instead soften the gradient slightly by reducing phi1 while keeping the successful 14 min length. This should expand the mid-late region where the critical cluster elutes, potentially improving resolution with minimal runtime increase.

Reducing phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the critical pair substantially at 14 min, suggesting a shallower effective gradient helps. A small increase to 16 min with the same endpoints is the most likely route to push the last pair over full-resolution while checking whether the time penalty remains modest enough to beat the current best.

The phi1 reduction to 0.90 improved selectivity at 14 min, but extending to 16 min incurred too much time penalty. Pushing phi1 one step lower at the faster 14 min setting should further ease the critical 6/7 pair while keeping runtime closer to the current optimum.

The critical congestion is in the middle of the chromatogram, and lowering phi1 helped but slightly lengthened the run. Raising phi0 one step while keeping the successful shallower span may trim early low-value time and could reposition the central cluster favorably enough to improve CRF further.

Raising phi0 to 0.10 improved runtime and overall CRF while keeping the same critical pair only slightly below 1.5. Lowering phi1 one step at this better starting composition may nudge that pair into full resolution with only a small time increase, offering a chance to reach the maximum score.

A nearby confirmatory variant is the safest different method now that the maximum score has been reached. Lowering phi1 one step should preserve full resolution while testing the edge of the zero-time-penalty region and the robustness of the optimum.

The optimum appears to sit near phi1 0.85 with the critical pair just comfortably resolved, so the most informative remaining local move is to raise phi0 one step. This may shorten the early portion and maintain full separation, testing whether another 1.000-equivalent robust setting exists closer to the fast edge.

Raising phi0 from 0.10 to 0.15 preserved full resolution and improved speed while keeping a 1.000 CRF, so one more step higher is the most informative local test. This probes whether the optimum plateau extends further toward shorter retention without sacrificing the critical mid-cluster separation.

The data suggest a narrow optimum plateau: phi0 0.15 improved speed, but phi0 0.20 began to erode the critical 6/7 pair. Testing phi0 0.15 with a slightly stronger phi1 of 0.90 checks the other edge of that plateau and helps map robustness around the 1.000 region.

With phi0 fixed at 0.15, phi1 = 0.85 gives a 1.000 score while phi1 = 0.90 weakens the critical pair, so the remaining untested local neighbor is phi1 = 0.80. This checks the lower-phi1 edge of the optimum plateau and the robustness margin around the best condition.

Now that a robust 1.000 plateau is mapped near phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 0.85, the most informative remaining question is whether the same composition window can support a shorter gradient. Reducing tG to 12 min tests the fast edge directly and could reveal whether a still faster 1.000-equivalent method exists.

The 12 min test confirms the optimum is constrained by the 6/7 pair, so the 14 min methods are near the fast limit. A 16 min run at the best composition checks whether extra gradient time creates a broader full-resolution safety margin around the maximum-scoring condition.

Composition and gradient-time space are well mapped, with a clear 1.000 plateau near phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 0.85 at 14 min. A small temperature increase is a sensible orthogonal robustness check to see whether the maximum can be maintained or whether selectivity around the critical pair deteriorates.

The 45 C test at phi0 0.15 sharply worsened the critical pair, so a lower phi0 at the same temperature is the most useful follow-up to determine whether that temperature effect is global or can be offset by slightly weaker starting conditions. This maps thermal robustness around the known optimum with a single orthogonal adjustment.

Both 35 C and 45 C degraded selectivity near the optimum, suggesting 40 C may be close to ideal, but the lower-temperature side has not been checked at the best composition. Testing 30 C completes the temperature bracket and confirms whether the maximum-scoring method is also thermally robust only at 40 C.

With 40 C clearly optimal, the remaining value is to map one more composition corner near the fast edge of the known optimum region. Combining higher phi0 with lower phi1 tests whether a narrower, shallower span can preserve full resolution or whether phi0 0.20 is intrinsically beyond the selectivity limit.

The new 1.000 result at phi0 0.20, phi1 0.80 shows the optimum plateau extends further toward stronger starting conditions when phi1 is also lowered. One more step to phi0 0.25 tests the fast boundary of this plateau and may identify the most aggressive still-maximum method.

At phi0 0.25 the first two peaks collapsed, showing the front-end limit has been crossed; the next best local move is to keep phi0 at the successful 0.20 and lower phi1 one step. This tests whether the 1.000 plateau extends to an even shallower gradient span without triggering the early coelution seen at higher phi0.

A 1.000 plateau exists at phi0 0.20, phi1 0.80 and at 14 min the critical pair is comfortably resolved, so the last valuable optimization question is whether this composition can tolerate a shorter gradient. Testing 12 min here probes for a faster high-scoring variant near the best-performing corner of the mapped space.

The final untested high-value neighbor is the faster version of the well-resolved phi0 0.20, phi1 0.75 method. This last run checks whether the extra selectivity margin at phi1 0.75 is enough to retain full resolution at 12 min and potentially finish very near the optimum.
